contrasts.title: Bet or vet (b / v)
contrasts.prompt: Which sound is the marked letter?
contrasts.note: The same letter: with a dagesh dot it is b, without it is v. Real in every tradition, so a browser voice can carry it.

contrasts.title: Het or khaf
contrasts.note: In Israeli Hebrew, and in the browser voice, het and khaf sound the same (a throaty kh), so this is a spelling check, not a listening one. Mizrahi, Yemenite and some Sephardi speakers pronounce het deeper in the throat; only a recording in such a voice would make it a true listening drill.

contrasts.title: Kamatz: a or o

sounds.label: o as in "more" (kamatz katan or cholam)

contrasts.prompt: Is the vowel after the marked letter a or o?
contrasts.note: Kamatz is usually a, but kamatz katan is o and looks the same in print. Ashkenazi reading says o for every kamatz. The browser voice may read a kamatz katan as a: only a recorded clip can be trusted for those words.

contrasts.title: Shin or sin (sh / s)

sounds.label: sh as in "ship" (dot on the right)
s as in "sun" (dot on the left)

contrasts.prompt: Which sound is the marked letter?
contrasts.note: Same letter, two sounds, told apart by which side the dot sits on. Real in every tradition.
